run_profile.applies_to: every arm run that invokes izyan analyze / izyan eval vex-bench (B0 re-verification, PR1 inputs, repeat-stability samples); pinned in the identical-conditions checklist (protocol.md §2, §10)
run_profile.parallelism_upper_bound: -j <= 3 — the verified baseline profile is -j 3; higher parallelism is an unverified profile
run_profile.mem_limit: --mem-limit 24GiB — the ceiling is result-affecting (eval/agent7/proof-feasibility.md §7: INCONCLUSIVE at -j 2 --mem-limit 8GiB vs EXPLOITABLE at 24GiB on cilium-cilium-3977f6a); a different ceiling is a different profile, not a tuning knob
run_profile.guard_trip: a tripping memory guard (cmd/izyan/memguard.go) is a RUN-PROFILE failure, never a verdict and never an alternative profile
run_profile.guard_trip_detection: instant 'advisory error: osv get … context canceled' envelopes with wall_seconds ≈ 0 (17/30 cases in the invalidated j2/8GiB attempt), corroborated by the degraded 'limitations' marker; the marker alone is not a detector — the same strings appear in healthy runs — so exclusion is always an operator declaration, never inferred
run_profile.degraded_declaration: an arm run may not be scored while any case is infra or degraded; the generator's --require-complete refuses final artifacts in that state and --degraded <case_id> / --invalidated <run_dir> are the exclusion mechanism; every exclusion is recorded in the run manifest
run_profile.repeat_stability: ≥3 cases × 2 repeats on the same snapshot under the identical pinned profile with identical verdicts required before any arm comparison is scored; a mismatch blocks scoring and is reported, never averaged away
run_profile.advisory_reproducibility: live OSV responses are not canonical — byte digests of the same advisory differ in member order (ecosystem_specific.imports); matched arm comparison requires a frozen advisory snapshot or digest canonicalisation (run_gate E7); govulncheck's vulnerability DB is a separate egress path — a frozen vulndb or recorded db_info is required (run_gate E7b)

e6.status_contract: PASS = every probe assertion verified (gate opens); ENV_FAIL = environment/precondition failure, e.g. model provider unreachable while VPN was down — fail-closed, NOT an isolation violation; FAIL = an isolation/security assertion was violated — fail-closed. The report is produced by the agent-ctl e6-preflight (schema agent7-e6-probe/1); report_path pins the committed verbatim copy of the probe report (recorded 2026-10-11, 29/29 checks PASS) and report_sha256 pins its bytes (E6 sandbox design §5/§6)

sandbox.profile: e6 — the OS/container boundary every A2 B1/R0 attempt runs under (security-boundary-check.md §8); proven by the probe report pinned in environment.e6

docker.entrypoint: e6-exec-guard (absolute inside the container image: usr/local/bin/e6-exec-guard — recorded without the leading slash so host path rules do not misfire; see the probe report for the verbatim argv)
docker.env_policy: no env-file; cleared HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY; HOME=/tmp; XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/.config; no credentials in the container environment
docker.exec_guard: static Landlock LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_EXECUTE policy: exec allowed under image system paths only, denied under /work, /tmp, /run-output (probe: EACCES); noexec tmpfs is the second layer

dataset.note: the 30 Go VEX-Bench cases are a development/regression set, NOT a blind holdout (spec §9.3); per-case GT labels stay controller-side and are never committed (see gt_policy)

holdout.selection_protocol: independent curator selects and freezes the holdout before any inspection of agent answers; no overlap with the dev 30, VEX-Bench upstream or prior PRs; holdout data unreachable from model containers; frozen candidate prompt/tool-policy/checkers/scorer/budgets set before blind runs
holdout.note: protocol only, no data (spec §9.3, plan §A1/A9); the run gate requires the holdout manifest pinned before blind runs

checkpoint_0.question: start a custom research runtime at all?
criteria: A0 reuse audit completed: shadow base reproducible, research changes separable from core
GT isolation demonstrably holds (negative tests green, denied-path probe enforced)
proof lane potential from A1.5 known before any checker work
checkpoint_0.stop_rule: STOP proof if potential value absent; ADJUST environment if sandbox guarantees are unmet; GO research only when reuse + GT isolation hold

checkpoint_a.question: R0 vs B1 — measurable analyst usefulness?
criteria: research value — at least one of: (a) improvement >= 0.5 anchored points on vulnerability_mechanism OR root_cause AND >= 0.5 on one of alternative_paths / product_exposure / evidence_quality; (b) >= 25% reduction of median analyst time-to-decision without degradation of research quality

mandatory constraints: proposed_false_safe <= B1 at attempt level AND at case level; any new false-safe conclusion on a case that was previously handled correctly (exploitable) is a separate BLOCKING signal; output-contract compliance and completion success no worse than B1; execution cost <= 2x B1
aggregation rule: aggregate first across repeats within a CVE, then across cases; on 8-12 dev cases the result decides whether to continue the architecture, not whether it is safe
checkpoint_a.stop_rule: if R0 ~= B1 → keep plain coding-agent with minimal export; do not build custom runtime (plan §9 stop rule 1); the signed criteria above are the operator's decision thresholds — no post-hoc adjustment
checkpoint_a.signoff_source: operator sign-off message of 2026-10-11 (GO A2, thresholds as recorded above); provenance convention of docs/dev/decisions/agent7-checkpoint-0.md — no signature artifact exists

checkpoint_b.question: R1/R2 ablation — do tools and critic add utility?
criteria: R1 adds >=1 new correct observation (precision+recall gain or evidence discovery gain) over R0 on >=20% of cases, AND
R2 produces >=1 correct correction/counterexample over R1, AND
no increase in proposed_false_safe at comparable research quality
checkpoint_b.stop_rule: if R1/R2 add no facts/counterexamples or raise FS → remove the corresponding layer (plan §9 stop rule 2); tool count is never self-justifying

checkpoint_c.question: is a proof product needed?
criteria: incremental_safe_clear > 0 against independently re-verified B0 with practical value (operator-set minimum new verified safes), AND
zero accepted unsafe certificates on any evaluated case, AND
scope/preconditions confirmed and fault-injection fails closed
checkpoint_c.stop_rule: zero or near-zero increment → STOP the proof lane; research lane continues (plan §9 stop rule 3); no post-hoc threshold adjustment after seeing results

checkpoints.meta_rule: all thresholds are PROPOSED pending operator sign-off before the corresponding comparison runs; no post-hoc adjustment

attribution.cost_per_attempt: recorded per attempt key (tokens in/out, wall-clock, container minutes)
attribution.cost_per_case: aggregated over the case's attempts; case-level and attempt-level denominators kept separate — 3 repeats of one case are not 3 independent cases
attribution.cost_per_new_verified_safe: total lane cost / incremental_safe_clear numerator; reported per proof type
attribution.baseline_certified_source: independently re-verified B0 outputs recorded as AttemptRecord{certificate_source: baseline_b0} — never old verdict labels and never committed per-case ids
